claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1C and is consistent with previous findings (Adamson et al., 2016).

claims.claim: Efficient activation of IRE1α in Sec61-depleted cells typically required treatment with the ER stress inducer thapsigargin.
claims.source: However, an efficient activation of IRE1α in these cells typically required treatment with the ER stress inducer thapsigargin (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: The depletion of the Sec61 translocon specifically affected IRE1α complexes, as PERK complexes were less disrupted in Sec61 depleted cells relative to the control siRNA-depleted cells.
claims.source: Intriguingly, the depletion of the Sec61 translocon specifically affected IRE1α complexes, as PERK complexes were less disrupted in Sec61 depleted cells relative to the control siRNA-depleted cells (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: The Sec61 translocon ran predominantly as a ~146 kDa form and a minor ~350 kDa form on BN-PAGE.
claims.source: The Sec61 translocon, which is composed of α, β, and γ subunits, ran predominantly as a ~146 kDa form and a minor ~350 kDa form on BN-PAGE (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), which is consistent with previous studies (Conti et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and is consistent with previous studies (Conti et al., 2015).

claims.claim: Only a small population of the highly abundant Sec61 exists in a complex with IRE1α in cells.
claims.source: Currently, it is unclear why we were not able to detect Sec61 co-migration with IRE1α, though it is likely that only a small population of the highly abundant Sec61 exists in a complex with IRE1α in cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference to explain why Sec61 co-migration with IRE1α was not detected in BN-PAGE.

claims.claim: Purified IRE1α associated with the Sec61 translocon and Sec63.
claims.source: The coomassie blue stained gel revealed that purified IRE1α associated with the Sec61 translocon and Sec63, a component of the translocon complex (Figure 2A) (Meyer et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by coomassie blue staining data shown in Figure 2A and citation (Meyer et al., 2000).

claims.claim: wIRE1α lacked the Sec61 translocon complex.
claims.source: As expected, wIRE1α lacked the Sec61 translocon complex, whereas sIRE1α associated with the Sec61 translocon complex (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by coomassie blue staining data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: sIRE1α associated with the Sec61 translocon complex.
claims.source: As expected, wIRE1α lacked the Sec61 translocon complex, whereas sIRE1α associated with the Sec61 translocon complex (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by coomassie blue staining data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: All three IRE1α proteins had a similar ability to cleave in vitro transcribed XBP1u mRNA substrate, though wIRE1α and sIRE1α showed slightly slower kinetics of cleavage.
claims.source: All three IRE1α proteins had a similar ability to cleave in vitro transcribed XBP1u mRNA substrate, though wIRE1α and sIRE1α showed slightly slower kinetics of cleavage (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro cleavage assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Purified IRE1α existed as complexes of both Form A and Form B when it associated with the Sec61 translocon.
claims.source: Similar to the IRE1α complexes in cells, purified IRE1α existed as complexes of both Form A and Form B when it associated with the Sec61 translocon (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Purified wIRE1α existed predominantly as Form B and as a ~240 kDa complex.
claims.source: In contrast, the purified wIRE1α existed predominantly as Form B and as a ~240 kDa complex.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The 240 kDa form of IRE1α was not obvious in cells, suggesting that IRE1α complexes may be labile during the purification procedure.
claims.source: The 240 kDa form of IRE1α was not obvious in cells, suggesting that IRE1α complexes may be labile during the purification procedure.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the 240 kDa form is seen in purified protein but not in cells.

claims.claim: sIRE1α closely resembled the wild-type IRE1α complexes because both purified IRE1α and sIRE1α proteins contained similarly enriched Sec61 translocon complex.
claims.source: sIRE1α closely resembled the wild-type IRE1α complexes because both purified IRE1α and sIRE1α proteins contained similarly enriched Sec61 translocon complex (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Sec61 co-migrates with both Form A and Form B in purified IRE1α and sIRE1α.
claims.source: Remarkably, BN-PAGE analysis with Sec61α antibodies revealed that Sec61 co-migrates with both Form A and Form B in purified IRE1α and sIRE1α (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Sec61α was not detectable in BN-PAGE with the purified wIRE1α.
claims.source: In contrast, Sec61α was not detectable in BN-PAGE with the purified wIRE1α.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: BiP was not detected in purified IRE1α complexes.
claims.source: At present, the role of BiP, which is known to interact and inhibit IRE1α oligomerization (Bertolotti et al., 2000; Okamura et al., 2000; Oikawa et al., 2009; Carrara et al., 2015), in the Sec61 translocon-mediated regulation of IRE1α complexes is unclear, since we could not detect BiP in our purified IRE1α complexes (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: IRE1α and sIRE1α exist in Forms A and B with the Sec61 translocon, while wIRE1α is predominantly in Form B but without the Sec61 translocon.
claims.source: We find that IRE1α and sIRE1α exist in Forms A and B with the Sec61 translocon, while wIRE1α is predominantly in Form B but without the Sec61 translocon.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the BN-PAGE data from purified proteins.

claims.claim: Sec61 is an intrinsic part of the IRE1α complexes under normal and ER stress conditions.
claims.source: Although further work is required to determine the precise copy numbers of IRE1α in these complexes, our data suggest that Sec61 is an intrinsic part of the IRE1α complexes under normal and ER stress conditions.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the BN-PAGE data showing Sec61 co-migration with IRE1α complexes.

claims.claim: IRE1α forms higher-order oligomers or clusters upon ER stress, which correlate with IRE1α RNase activity.
claims.source: Previous studies reported that IRE1α forms higher-order oligomers or clusters upon ER stress, which correlate with IRE1α RNase activity and are proposed to be important for IRE1α signaling (Li et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Li et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Under normal conditions, IRE1α and wIRE1α were diffusely distributed in the ER membrane and colocalized with Sec61β.
claims.source: Under normal conditions, IRE1α and wIRE1α were diffusely distributed in the ER membrane and colocalized with Sec61β, a subunit of the Sec61 translocon (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Robust clusters were detected with wIRE1α expressing cells but not in wild-type IRE1α expressing cells upon treatment with tunicamycin.
claims.source: Strikingly, we detected robust clusters with wIRE1α expressing cells but not in wild-type IRE1α expressing cells upon treatment with tunicamycin, which induces ER stress by inhibiting protein glycosylation in the ER (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Clusters were not observed in sIRE1α expressing cells upon treatment with tunicamycin.
claims.source: Similar to wild-type IRE1α, we failed to observe clusters in sIRE1α expressing cells (Figure 3A), supporting the idea that the IRE1α interaction with the Sec61 translocon limits cluster formation.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The IRE1α interaction with the Sec61 translocon limits cluster formation.
claims.source: Similar to wild-type IRE1α, we failed to observe clusters in sIRE1α expressing cells (Figure 3A), supporting the idea that the IRE1α interaction with the Sec61 translocon limits cluster formation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that sIRE1α, which binds strongly to Sec61, does not form clusters.

claims.claim: wIRE1α clustering was not dependent on cell types since similar results were obtained in IRE1α-/- MEF cells.
claims.source: wIRE1α clustering was not dependent on cell types since we obtained similar results when we analyzed IRE1α-/- mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) cells complemented with either wild-type or wIRE1α (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: ER stress-mediated clusters of wIRE1α were not unique to the wIRE1α mutant with a ten amino acid deletion, but were also observed in cells expressing a wIRE1α mutant where two critical residues are mutated within the ten amino acid region.
claims.source: In addition, ER stress-mediated clusters of wIRE1α were not unique to this particular wIRE1α mutant, which has a ten amino acid deletion in IRE1α, but were also observed in cells expressing a wIRE1α mutant where two critical residues are mutated within the ten amino acid region (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claims.claim: A small percentage of clusters in wild-type IRE1α expressing cells were detected only after increasing the expression level of IRE1α using doxycycline.
claims.source: Only after increasing the expression level of IRE1α using doxycycline, could we detect a small percentage of clusters in wild-type IRE1α expressing cells (Figure 3B,C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B,C,D.

claims.claim: Robust wIRE1α clusters were detected in ER stress treated cells even at low expression levels.
claims.source: In contrast, we detected robust wIRE1α clusters in ER stress treated cells even at low expression levels.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3B,C,D.

claims.claim: The Sec61 translocon interaction prevents the formation of IRE1α higher order oligomers or clusters in cells.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that the Sec61 translocon interaction prevents the formation of IRE1α higher order oligomers or clusters in cells.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that wIRE1α, which lacks Sec61 interaction, forms more clusters than wild-type IRE1α.

claims.claim: Only a low percentage of cells containing wild-type IRE1α clusters were observed.
claims.source: In contrast with previous work (Li et al., 2010; Ghosh et al., 2014), we observe only a low percentage of cells containing wild-type IRE1α clusters.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data and quantification.

claims.claim: The difference in the percentage of cells with wild-type IRE1α clusters may be due to the intensity of ER stress applied to monitor IRE1α clusters in cells.
claims.source: This difference may be due to the intensity of ER stress applied to monitor IRE1α clusters in cells.
claims.evidence: This is speculation to explain the difference between the current study and previous work.

claims.claim: Overexpressed IRE1α was partially activated as shown by phosphorylation even in the absence of ER stress.
claims.source: Consistent with previous findings, overexpressed IRE1α was partially activated as shown by phosphorylation even in the absence of ER stress (Li et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4A,B and is consistent with previous findings (Li et al., 2010).

claims.claim: Overexpressed wIRE1α exhibited an even larger amount of auto-phosphorylation and thus activation compared to wild-type IRE1α.
claims.source: Overexpressed wIRE1α exhibited an even larger amount of auto-phosphorylation and thus activation compared to wild-type IRE1α, while overexpressed sIRE1α showed reduced auto-phosphorylation compared to wild-type IRE1α.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: Overexpressed sIRE1α showed reduced auto-phosphorylation compared to wild-type IRE1α.
claims.source: Overexpressed wIRE1α exhibited an even larger amount of auto-phosphorylation and thus activation compared to wild-type IRE1α, while overexpressed sIRE1α showed reduced auto-phosphorylation compared to wild-type IRE1α.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: All IRE1α variants required ER stress treatment to achieve a full activation state.
claims.source: Interestingly, all IRE1α variants required ER stress treatment, in this case thapsigargin, to achieve a full activation state, suggesting that the accumulation of misfolded proteins plays a major role in IRE1α activation (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: The accumulation of misfolded proteins plays a major role in IRE1α activation.
claims.source: Interestingly, all IRE1α variants required ER stress treatment, in this case thapsigargin, to achieve a full activation state, suggesting that the accumulation of misfolded proteins plays a major role in IRE1α activation (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that ER stress treatment is required for full IRE1α activation.

claims.claim: wIRE1α was more quickly activated as shown by auto-phosphorylation compared to the wild type.
claims.source: Consistently, wIRE1α was more quickly activated as shown by auto-phosphorylation compared to the wild type, whereas sIRE1α was activated at slower rate during ER stress (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claims.claim: sIRE1α was activated at slower rate during ER stress.
claims.source: Consistently, wIRE1α was more quickly activated as shown by auto-phosphorylation compared to the wild type, whereas sIRE1α was activated at slower rate during ER stress (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claims.claim: PERK was activated similarly in all three IRE1α variants expressing cells.
claims.source: As a control, we probed for the activation of PERK, which was activated similarly in all three IRE1α variants expressing cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The proper activation of IRE1α relies on an interaction with the Sec61 translocon.
claims.source: Taken together, our results suggest that the proper activation of IRE1α relies on an interaction with the Sec61 translocon.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the differential activation kinetics of IRE1α variants with different Sec61 binding affinities.

claims.claim: IRE1α was fully activated after two hours of ER stress treatment as demonstrated by all IRE1α shifting to the phosphorylated state.
claims.source: IRE1α was fully activated after two hours of ER stress treatment as demonstrated by all IRE1α shifting to the phosphorylated state (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: Spliced XBP1 (XBP1s) protein production peaked at five hours.
claims.source: Spliced XBP1 (XBP1s) protein production peaked at five hours.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: During prolonged stress, IRE1α was gradually inactivated with a concomitant reduction in the production of spliced XBP1 protein (XBP1s).
claims.source: During prolonged stress, IRE1α was gradually inactivated with a concomitant reduction in the production of spliced XBP1 protein (XBP1s) (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting and XBP1s immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: PERK was activated through the duration of the stress period.
claims.source: Unlike IRE1α, PERK was activated through the duration of the stress period.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: IRE1α-mediated XBP1u mRNA splicing diminished within a few hours of stress despite the continuation of the ER stress treatment.
claims.source: This is consistent with previous studies which showed that IRE1α-mediated XBP1u mRNA splicing diminished within a few hours of stress despite the continuation of the ER stress treatment (Lin et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Lin et al., 2007).

claims.claim: wIRE1α showed significantly reduced inactivation as well as extended production of XBP1s during prolonged ER stress.
claims.source: In sharp contrast to wild-type IRE1α, the Sec61 interaction-defective mutant, wIRE1α, showed significantly reduced inactivation as well as extended production of XBP1s during prolonged ER stress (Figure 5A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting and XBP1s immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claims.claim: A similar difference in IRE1α and wIRE1α phosphorylation was observed with tunicamycin.
claims.source: A similar difference in IRE1α and wIRE1α phosphorylation was observed with tunicamycin (Figure 5C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claims.claim: IRE1α was nearly completely inactivated during prolonged tunicamycin treatment, but wIRE1α was only partially inactivated.
claims.source: Here, IRE1α was nearly completely inactivated, but wIRE1α was only partially inactivated during prolonged stress.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5C,D.

claims.claim: The temporal inactivation of IRE1α during ER stress was not specific to the complemented recombinant IRE1α since a similar result was obtained with the endogenous IRE1α in HEK293 cells.
claims.source: The temporal inactivation of IRE1α during ER stress was not specific to the complemented recombinant IRE1α since we obtained a similar result with the endogenous IRE1α in HEK293 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Under ER stress treatment conditions when both IRE1α and wIRE1α are equally activated, wIRE1α cells produced less XBP1s protein.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous work, under ER stress treatment conditions when both IRE1α and wIRE1α are equally activated, wIRE1α cells produced less XBP1s protein (Figure 5A,C and five hour treatment) since the lack of the Sec61 translocon interaction prevented efficient XBP1u mRNA cleavage (Plumb et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A,C and is consistent with previous work (Plumb et al., 2015).

claims.claim: Production of XBP1s-induced proteins, such as BiP and the Sec61 translocon, were similar in both IRE1α and wIRE1α expressing cells.
claims.source: However, we found that production of XBP1s-induced proteins, such as BiP and the Sec61 translocon, were similar in both IRE1α and wIRE1α expressing cells (Figure 5A,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5A,C.

claims.claim: Despite the overexpression of XBP1s, wIRE1α was still attenuated significantly slower than wild-type IRE1α.
claims.source: Despite the overexpression of XBP1s, wIRE1α was still attenuated significantly slower than wild-type IRE1α (Figure 5E,F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claims.claim: sIRE1α showed a faster inactivation rate during prolonged ER stress conditions.
claims.source: Indeed, sIRE1α showed a faster inactivation rate during prolonged ER stress conditions (Figure 5G,H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5G,H.

claims.claim: The presence of misfolded proteins in the ER is required for the continuous activation of wIRE1α.
claims.source: Halting protein synthesis after removing ER stress allowed for complete inactivation of wIRE1α similar to IRE1α and PERK (Figure 5—figure supplement 2). This result implies that the presence of misfolded proteins in the ER is required for the continuous activation of wIRE1α.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: An efficient inactivation of IRE1α requires the IRE1α interaction with the Sec61 translocon.
claims.source: Together, these results indicate that an efficient inactivation of IRE1α requires the IRE1α interaction with the Sec61 translocon.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the differential inactivation kinetics of IRE1α variants with different Sec61 binding affinities.

claims.claim: High concentration of thapsigargin induced clusters in IRE1α, wIRE1α, and sIRE1α expressing cells.
claims.source: This high concentration of thapsigargin, but not a lower concentration, induced clusters in IRE1α, wIRE1α, and sIRE1α expressing cells, though a higher percentage of wIRE1α cells presented clusters than wild-type IRE1α or sIRE1α cells (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: A higher percentage of wIRE1α cells presented clusters than wild-type IRE1α or sIRE1α cells under severe ER stress.
claims.source: This high concentration of thapsigargin, but not a lower concentration, induced clusters in IRE1α, wIRE1α, and sIRE1α expressing cells, though a higher percentage of wIRE1α cells presented clusters than wild-type IRE1α or sIRE1α cells (Figure 6A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: The Sec61-IRE1α complex plays a role in limiting IRE1α oligomerization under ER stress conditions, but increased misfolded protein accumulation during severe ER stress conditions overcomes the Sec61 translocon-mediated restriction of IRE1α oligomerization.
claims.source: These results suggest that the Sec61-IRE1α complex plays a role in limiting IRE1α oligomerization under ER stress conditions, but increased misfolded protein accumulation during severe ER stress conditions overcomes the Sec61 translocon-mediated restriction of IRE1α oligomerization.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that severe ER stress induces clusters even in wild-type IRE1α.

claims.claim: The interaction between IRE1α and the Sec61 translocon was little changed during both medial and severe ER stress conditions.
claims.source: Interestingly, the interaction between IRE1α and the Sec61 translocon was little changed during both medial and severe ER stress conditions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The endogenous Sec61 translocon co-localized with IRE1α clusters in both wild type IRE1α and sIRE1α expressing cells.
claims.source: Consistent with our hypothesis, confocal imaging revealed that the endogenous Sec61 translocon co-localized with IRE1α clusters in both wild type IRE1α and sIRE1α expressing cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: wIRE1α clusters appear to lack the Sec61 translocon.
claims.source: However, wIRE1α clusters appear to lack the Sec61 translocon (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The attenuation of wild-type IRE1α during severe stress was significantly delayed compared to less severe stress.
claims.source: Indeed, the attenuation of wild-type IRE1α during severe stress was significantly delayed compared to less severe stress.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data shown in Figure 6C,D.

claims.claim: The production of spliced XBP1 mRNA and its protein were continued during severe ER stress.
claims.source: Thus, the production of spliced XBP1 mRNA and its protein were continued (Figure 6C,D and E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting and XBP1 splicing assay data shown in Figure 6C,D,E.

claims.claim: Once IRE1α forms higher oligomers, due to either a defect in the interaction with Sec61 or under severe ER stress, it becomes resistant to inactivation.
claims.source: These results suggest that once IRE1α forms higher oligomers, due to either a defect in the interaction with Sec61 or under severe ER stress, it becomes resistant to inactivation.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that both wIRE1α and wild-type IRE1α under severe stress show delayed inactivation.

claims.claim: IRE1α oligomerization and RNAse activity are limited by the Sec61 translocon during normal and remedial ER stress levels.
claims.source: We find that IRE1α oligomerization and RNAse activity are limited by the Sec61 translocon during normal and remedial ER stress levels, but that severe ER stress overcomes this block, resulting in prolonged IRE1α activation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claims.claim: Severe ER stress overcomes the Sec61 translocon-mediated block on IRE1α oligomerization, resulting in prolonged IRE1α activation.
claims.source: We find that IRE1α oligomerization and RNAse activity are limited by the Sec61 translocon during normal and remedial ER stress levels, but that severe ER stress overcomes this block, resulting in prolonged IRE1α activation.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claims.claim: The IRE1α-Sec61 complex plays an important role in measuring ER stress levels and accordingly tuning IRE1α activity.
claims.source: Our results point to an important role for the IRE1α-Sec61 complex in measuring ER stress levels and accordingly tuning IRE1α activity, which may determine cell fate during ER stress.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the findings that the Sec61-IRE1α interaction regulates IRE1α activity in a stress-dependent manner.

claims.claim: The IRE1α-Sec61 complex may determine cell fate during ER stress.
claims.source: Our results point to an important role for the IRE1α-Sec61 complex in measuring ER stress levels and accordingly tuning IRE1α activity, which may determine cell fate during ER stress.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the broader implications of the findings.

claims.claim: IRE1α appears to be in preassembled complexes during steady-state conditions.
claims.source: To our surprise, we found that IRE1α appears to be in preassembled complexes during steady-state conditions.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BN-PAGE data showing IRE1α complexes in unstressed cells.

claims.claim: IRE1α activation is most likely caused by a conformational change induced within the preformed IRE1α complexes by binding with misfolded proteins in the lumen.
claims.source: This result suggests that IRE1α activation is most likely caused by a conformational change induced within the preformed IRE1α complexes by binding with misfolded proteins in the lumen.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that IRE1α complexes change little upon ER stress but IRE1α becomes activated.

claims.claim: The extreme low-abundance of IRE1α might result in a very slow rate of oligomer formation and activation.
claims.source: We propose that the extreme low-abundance of IRE1α (Plumb et al., 2015; Kulak et al., 2014) might result in a very slow rate of oligomer formation and activation.
claims.evidence: This is speculation based on the low abundance of IRE1α and the observation of preassembled complexes.

claims.claim: Preassembled IRE1α complexes may be essential for the rapid and robust IRE1α activation observed in cells.
claims.source: Thus, preassembled IRE1α complexes may be essential for the rapid and robust IRE1α activation observed in cells.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the functional significance of preassembled IRE1α complexes.

claims.claim: Wild-type IRE1α forms clusters under severe ER stress conditions.
claims.source: In accordance with previous reports, we find that wild-type IRE1α forms clusters, though we only observe significant cluster formation under severe ER stress conditions.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing IRE1α clusters under high thapsigargin treatment.

claims.claim: wIRE1α formed robust clusters during remediable ER stress conditions.
claims.source: In contrast, wIRE1α formed robust clusters during remediable ER stress conditions and exhibited a higher percentage of clusters than IRE1α during severe stress conditions.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data showing wIRE1α clusters under moderate ER stress.

claims.claim: The Sec61 translocon limits IRE1α cluster formation.
claims.source: These data suggest that the Sec61 translocon limits IRE1α cluster formation and that the preassembled complexes of wIRE1α may collide and form clusters rapidly in the absence of the Sec61 interaction.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that wIRE1α, which lacks Sec61 interaction, forms more clusters.

claims.claim: The preassembled complexes of wIRE1α may collide and form clusters rapidly in the absence of the Sec61 interaction.
claims.source: These data suggest that the Sec61 translocon limits IRE1α cluster formation and that the preassembled complexes of wIRE1α may collide and form clusters rapidly in the absence of the Sec61 interaction.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of wIRE1α cluster formation.

claims.claim: The Sec61 translocon-mediated restriction of IRE1α oligomerization may be overcome under severe ER stress conditions.
claims.source: Severe ER stress drastically increases cluster formation in cells expressing wild-type IRE1α, suggesting that the Sec61 translocon-mediated restriction of IRE1α oligomerization may be overcome under these conditions.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that severe ER stress induces clusters in wild-type IRE1α.

claims.claim: Severe ER stress increases the number of misfolded polypeptides in the ER, which may overcome the Sec61 barrier and drive the IRE1α and Sec61 complexes into clusters.
claims.source: One potential explanation is that severe ER stress increases the number of misfolded polypeptides in the ER, which may overcome the Sec61 barrier and drive the IRE1α and Sec61 complexes into clusters.
claims.evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism by which severe ER stress overcomes the Sec61 barrier.

claims.claim: Misfolded proteins can directly bind and activate yeast IRE1α.
claims.source: This is supported by previous studies that indicate misfolded proteins can directly bind and activate yeast IRE1α (Kimata et al., 2007; Gardner and Walter, 2011), though the similar evidence is currently lacking in metazoans (Oikawa et al., 2012).

results.result: IRE1α exists as preassembled hetero-oligomeric complexes (Form A ~500 kDa and Form B ~720 kDa) that undergo minimal structural changes upon ER stress activation. BN-PAGE analysis shows that upon ER stress, Form B slightly increases while Form A decreases, with IRE1α becoming phosphorylated. In contrast, PERK shows dramatic complex size changes from ~900 kDa to ~1200 kDa upon stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C56 and C126 are well-supported by BN-PAGE immunoblotting data (Figure 1A, 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2) showing IRE1α complexes before and after ER stress treatment in multiple cell types. The phos-tag assays (C49, C52) confirm activation despite minimal complex changes. The contrast with PERK's behavior (C53-C56) strengthens the conclusion that IRE1α's unique activation mechanism involves conformational changes within preassembled complexes.

results.result: Sec61 translocon depletion causes wild-type IRE1α to shift from Form A to Form B, mimicking the wIRE1α mutant (Δ434-443) that lacks Sec61 interaction. Sec61 depletion partially activates IRE1α under basal conditions but requires ER stress for full activation. This effect is specific to IRE1α, as PERK complexes are less affected by Sec61 depletion.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 are supported by BN-PAGE data (Figure 1C, 1D) showing that siRNA-mediated Sec61 depletion causes wild-type IRE1α to resemble wIRE1α in complex formation. The specificity for IRE1α over PERK (C61) and the requirement for ER stress for full activation (C60) are demonstrated experimentally. The genetic validation using the wIRE1α mutant (C43) provides strong support for the Sec61-IRE1α interaction's role in complex regulation.

results.result: Purified IRE1α and sIRE1α associate with the Sec61 translocon and Sec63, existing as both Form A and Form B complexes with Sec61 co-migrating in both forms. In contrast, purified wIRE1α lacks Sec61 and exists predominantly as Form B and a ~240 kDa complex. All three IRE1α variants show similar in vitro RNase activity, though wIRE1α and sIRE1α have slightly slower cleavage kinetics. BiP was not detected in purified IRE1α complexes.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C76 are supported by biochemical purification data (Figure 2A-D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1). Coomassie staining and BN-PAGE with Sec61α antibodies (C72) directly demonstrate Sec61 co-migration with IRE1α complexes. The absence of BiP in purified complexes (C74) is clearly shown but leaves open questions about BiP's role. The in vitro RNase assays (C67) validate that the mutations don't fundamentally impair catalytic activity, supporting the interpretation that observed differences in cells reflect regulatory mechanisms rather than intrinsic enzymatic defects.

results.result: The Sec61 translocon limits IRE1α cluster formation during ER stress. wIRE1α forms robust clusters upon tunicamycin treatment, while wild-type IRE1α and sIRE1α do not form clusters under the same conditions. Wild-type IRE1α only forms clusters at high expression levels or under severe ER stress. This phenotype is cell-type independent and occurs with multiple wIRE1α mutants.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C87, C130-C132 are supported by extensive immunofluorescence data (Figure 3A-D, Figure 3—figure supplements 1-2). Quantification shows clear differences in cluster formation between IRE1α variants (C84-C85). The cell-type independence (C82) and validation with alternative wIRE1α mutants (C83) strengthen the conclusion. However, the discrepancy with previous literature (C87-C88) regarding wild-type IRE1α cluster frequency is acknowledged but not fully resolved, suggesting stress intensity differences may explain the variation.

results.result: Proper IRE1α activation kinetics depend on Sec61 interaction. Overexpressed wIRE1α shows increased basal phosphorylation and faster activation during ER stress compared to wild-type IRE1α, while sIRE1α shows reduced basal phosphorylation and slower activation. All variants require ER stress for full activation, suggesting misfolded protein accumulation is essential. PERK activation is similar across all cell lines, serving as a control.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C97 are supported by phos-tag immunoblotting data (Figure 4A-D) showing differential activation kinetics. The dose-response experiments (C89-C91) and time-course analyses (C94-C95) provide quantitative support. The requirement for ER stress for full activation (C92-C93) is clearly demonstrated. The PERK control (C96) validates that the effects are specific to IRE1α. The inference that Sec61 interaction regulates proper activation (C97) is well-supported by the convergent data from multiple mutants.

results.result: Efficient IRE1α inactivation during prolonged ER stress requires Sec61 interaction. Wild-type IRE1α is fully activated at 2 hours and gradually inactivated during prolonged stress, while wIRE1α shows significantly delayed inactivation and extended XBP1s production. sIRE1α shows faster inactivation than wild-type. This phenotype is observed with both thapsigargin and tunicamycin, in recombinant and endogenous IRE1α, and is independent of XBP1s levels. Misfolded protein presence is required for sustained wIRE1α activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C112 are extensively supported by time-course experiments using phos-tag immunoblotting and XBP1s detection (Figure 5A-H, Figure 5—figure supplements 1-2). The differential inactivation kinetics between IRE1α variants are clearly demonstrated and quantified (C103-C105, C110). The XBP1s overexpression control (C109) rules out feedback regulation as the mechanism. The cycloheximide chase experiment (C111, Figure 5—figure supplement 2) demonstrates that ongoing protein misfolding is required for sustained wIRE1α activation. The consistency across multiple ER stress inducers and cell types strengthens the conclusions.

results.result: Severe ER stress (high thapsigargin concentration) overcomes Sec61-mediated restriction of IRE1α oligomerization, inducing clusters in wild-type IRE1α, wIRE1α, and sIRE1α, though wIRE1α shows the highest percentage. Under severe stress, wild-type IRE1α shows delayed inactivation and continued XBP1 mRNA splicing. The IRE1α-Sec61 interaction is maintained during both moderate and severe ER stress, and Sec61 co-localizes with IRE1α clusters (but not wIRE1α clusters) during severe stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C121, C123, C134 are supported by immunofluorescence data (Figure 6A-B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2), phos-tag immunoblotting (Figure 6C-D), and co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1). The dose-dependent effect of thapsigargin on cluster formation is clearly demonstrated. The maintenance of IRE1α-Sec61 interaction during stress (C116) and Sec61 co-localization with wild-type but not wIRE1α clusters (C117-C118) provide mechanistic insight. The delayed inactivation under severe stress (C119-C120) parallels the wIRE1α phenotype, supporting the model that higher-order oligomers resist inactivation.

results.result: The Sec61-IRE1α complex regulates IRE1α oligomerization, activation, and inactivation during ER stress, defining the extent of IRE1α activity. Loss of this interaction or severe ER stress causes higher-order oligomer formation with continuous activation. The authors propose that the Sec61-IRE1α complex measures ER stress levels and tunes IRE1α activity accordingly, potentially determining cell fate decisions.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C6, C122, C124-C125, C147-C148, C154, C160 represent the main conclusions synthesized from all experimental results. The regulatory role of Sec61 in IRE1α oligomerization, activation, and inactivation (C3, C122) is well-supported by the convergent evidence from BN-PAGE, immunofluorescence, and phosphorylation studies. The formation of higher-order oligomers with continuous activation upon loss of Sec61 interaction (C4-C5) is demonstrated through wIRE1α experiments. However, the proposals about cell fate determination (C6, C125) remain speculative as no cell death or survival assays are presented. The model is internally consistent and well-supported by the data, though some mechanistic details remain to be elucidated.

results.result: The authors propose that IRE1α activation occurs through conformational changes within preassembled complexes rather than de novo oligomerization, potentially because IRE1α's low abundance would result in slow oligomer formation. They speculate that preassembled complexes enable rapid activation, that wIRE1α complexes may collide to form clusters in the absence of Sec61, that severe stress increases misfolded proteins to overcome the Sec61 barrier, and that wIRE1α forms large oligomers sustaining prolonged activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C127-C129, C133, C135, C149 are mechanistic speculations based on the experimental observations but lack direct experimental validation. While the preassembled complex observation (C126) is well-supported, the proposed mechanisms for activation (C127), the functional significance of preassembly (C128-C129), and the collision model for wIRE1α clustering (C133) are reasonable inferences but remain untested. The speculation about misfolded proteins overcoming the Sec61 barrier (C135) is plausible but not directly demonstrated. These represent logical hypotheses for future investigation rather than established findings.

results.result: The Sec61 interaction prevents inappropriate IRE1α activation under basal conditions, as evidenced by wIRE1α's constitutive activation, increased ER stress sensitivity, and prolonged activity. This is consistent with findings that Sec61 depletion activates IRE1α signaling. Both BiP and Sec61 likely maintain IRE1α in an inactive state under normal conditions, but unlike BiP (which is released during stress), the Sec61 interaction is maintained throughout ER stress. Other IRE1α-interacting proteins besides Sec61 likely contribute to regulation. During prolonged stress, increased wIRE1α activation compensates for its reduced XBP1u mRNA access efficiency, resulting in greater XBP1s production than wild-type.
results.evaluation: Claims C138-C146, C150-C153 are supported by the experimental data and literature citations. The constitutive activation of wIRE1α (C139-C140) is demonstrated by phos-tag assays. The consistency with Sec61 depletion studies (C141) and BiP mutant phenotypes (C143) from the literature strengthens the interpretation. The maintenance of Sec61 interaction during stress (C146) is directly shown by co-IP experiments (Figure 6—figure supplements 1-2). The inference about other regulatory proteins (C150) is reasonable given that wIRE1α is eventually inactivated. The explanation for XBP1s production differences (C151-C153) reconciles apparent contradictions between this and previous work, though the quantitative relationship could be more rigorously demonstrated.

results.result: The authors speculate that selective IRE1α attenuation may benefit secretory cells by providing time to resolve ER stress and avoiding inappropriate mRNA cleavage, while severe stress-induced higher-order oligomers may cause defective attenuation. They propose that continuous IRE1α activation might benefit tumor growth but promote death in secretory cells like pancreatic beta cells, and that the IRE1α-Sec61 complex may be a therapeutic target.
results.evaluation: Claims C155-C159, C161 are speculations about physiological and pathological implications supported only by literature citations, not by experiments in this study. No cell death, survival, or disease-relevant assays are presented. While the speculation about secretory cell protection (C155) is reasonable given the RIDD mechanism, and the citations about tumor growth (C158) and beta cell death (C159) are appropriate, these remain untested hypotheses in the context of the Sec61-IRE1α interaction. The therapeutic potential (C161) is highly speculative without any drug studies or disease models.

results.result: The manuscript provides extensive background on ER protein folding, quality control, ER stress, the UPR, IRE1α structure and function, XBP1 mRNA splicing, RIDD, IRE1α regulation, and previous findings about IRE1α-Sec61 interaction. These claims establish the scientific context and rationale for the current study.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C7-C42, C62-C63, C70, C74, C77, C88, C102, C136-C137, C142 are background knowledge claims supported by appropriate literature citations or represent statements about the current state of knowledge in the field. These are generally well-established facts or previous findings from the authors' own work (C1, C25-C26, C39-C41) and others. Some claims acknowledge uncertainties in the field (C35, C63, C70, C74) which is appropriate. The citation to previous work on IRE1α clusters (C77) provides context for the current findings, and the acknowledgment of differences with previous studies (C88) is scientifically honest.
